lean.statement:
theorem anonymous
    {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (μ : Measure A) [SFinite μ]
    (R : Kernel A B) [IsSFiniteKernel R]
    (F : Kernel (A × B) B) [IsSFiniteKernel F]
    (hF : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, (F.comap (fun b => (a, b))
      (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_id)).IsReversible (R a)) :
    ((Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F).IsReversible (μ ⊗ₘ R)
approved_definition_context: Kernel X Y is a measurable map to nonnegative measures: for every measurable S in Y, x maps to kappa(x)(S) measurably. No Markov or finite-mass premise is part of this type.
SFinite on a measure means it is a countable sum of finite measures. IsSFiniteKernel is the analogous countable-sum condition for kernels. Neither class asserts probability normalization.

For a measurable map g, kappa.comap g is the kernel x maps to kappa(g(x)). Kernel.deterministic g is x maps to dirac(g(x)). Kernel product gives the independent product of its two output measures at the same input.
For s-finite mu and R, mu compProd R is the measure integrating a joint nonnegative measurable f as the iterated integral of f(a,b) against R(a) then mu.

IsReversible kappa pi means: for every pair of measurable sets S,T, the nonnegative integral over S of kappa(x)(T) against pi equals the analogous integral over T of kappa(x)(S). The definition itself has no Markov premise.
The notation forall-a.e. uses the measure ae filter; output flux integrals are extended nonnegative integrals, not totalized real Bochner integrals.
